limitations: The source is a fictional Handbook HTTP v1 laboratory; real corporate source behavior and ACL mapping are not verified.
Source rights can remain usable until the last successful snapshot confirmation expires (60 to 86400 seconds from sync start).
Listing consistency and immutable revision contents are source-contract assumptions; there is no global snapshot ID or ETag.
An OS resolver may outlive a timed-out caller; at most four process-wide daemon network workers may remain occupied.
Source deletion closes access to all versions but does not physically erase historical version bodies.
Downgrade deactivates mirrors and their grants; re-upgrade cannot restore source ownership without trusted preparation.
The offline provider quotes retrieved passages; it does not reason.
Every tool call is a full permission-filtered search; latency grows with calls and project size.
The agent loop cannot interrupt a blocking model provider; a live provider must apply its own timeout.
No rate limit per agent or employee; the synchronous answer route holds a worker for the whole run.
Question and query digests in history can be guessed for short inputs.
Bearer tokens impersonate their agent until expiry or revocation; memory HTTP is loopback only.
Database owners can modify documents, grants, credentials and history directly.
The Compose laboratory and the temporary native PostgreSQL lab are not a deployed service.
Evaluations cover only the listed behaviors; grounded-quote checks fit the offline provider only.
Drills need database-owner access and show detection, not prevention.
A restored source confirmation keeps aging; synced documents close after max_age until the next sync.
Latency figures come from one laptop and a few fictional documents; they are not a capacity claim.
The service role reads every document version and credential hash of its database; company isolation is enforced by the application.
Secrets are host files without rotation; Docker Desktop may need AGENTIC_SECRETS_DIR outside protected macOS folders.
Images still contain HIGH and CRITICAL findings without a released fix; the scan gate can fail when upstream fixes appear.
